author: Wil Day
title: Don't disturb Bambi: Baby deer season begins in Kansas - NewsBreak
text:
By Wil Day ,
11 hours ago
WICHITA, Kan. (KSNW) — Game wardens with the Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks want to remind everyone as they head out to enjoy nature that it’s “Baby Deer” season.
Over the next few weeks, an increasing number of does will be giving birth to their fawns.
During the first week of their life, fawns will bed down on the ground by themselves and stay still, even with humans and other animals around. After that first week, for up to 30 days, the fawns will continue to bed down but will run if they are startled and find a new spot on the ground or a place to hide.
Monarch tagged at Great Plains Nature Center completes migration journey to Mexico You may also hear them cry or bleat for their mother. The mother is usually close by, so Wildlife and Parks urges you not to disturb them or pick them up and to call the game warden instead.
If an officer shows up to pick up the deer you picked up, they will most likely just take it right back to the same spot and release it. This is their best chance of survival.
SO, please enjoy nature’s beauty at a distance.
Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks Game Wardens Nationwide fawn birth season typically starts in late April to early May and usually peaks in summer, according to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service .
